title: Windows Update fails or gets stuck (0x80070002, 0x800f0922, 0x80073712)
summary: An update keeps failing, restarts and rolls back, or sits at the same percentage for hours. Repairing Windows' update files fixes most cases.
cause: The update cache or Windows' own system files are damaged, or there isn't enough free space to install.
steps: Free up space. Aim for at least 10 GB free on your C: drive, and unplug USB drives and other extras you don't need.
Run the built-in fixer: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Update > Run. Restart afterward.

Open Terminal (Admin): right-click Start and choose Terminal (Admin). Type DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth and press Enter. When it finishes, type sfc /scannow and press Enter. Restart when both are done.

Reset the update cache. Open Terminal (Admin) and run these one at a time, pressing Enter after each: net stop wuauserv, net stop cryptSvc, net stop bits, net stop msiserver, ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old, ren C:\Windows\System32\catroot2 catroot2.old, net start wuauserv, net start cryptSvc, net start bits, net start msiserver. If Windows says a .old folder already exists, delete that old folder first (or end the name with .old2) and run the line again.
Restart, then go to Settings > Windows Update and click Check for updates.
ifStillBroken: Look up the failing update's KB number in Settings > Windows Update > Update history and install it by hand from the Microsoft Update Catalog (link below). Or send your error to OldWolfDev for a personal review.

links.note: Search the KB number to download an update manually.
